title: Cap. VI Arg. 9: Prosper on infants; Grevinchovius — if eternal life, then election
pass_a_gloss: To which Prosper assents in the book On Free Choice: In infants neither preceding nor following devotion is elected. I speak of those who as soon as they are born are reborn, and snatched from this life are assigned to eternal beatitude. Grevinchovius in the Disputation on Election from foresighted faith, p. 143, entangled by this argument, at last slips so far as to call into doubt whether there is any election of infants or not. But of those whose is eternal life, of them without doubt is election to eternal life, since the number of the glorified does not exceed the number of the predestinated or elect. For whom he predestinated, them he glorified, and not others, as Augustine rightly expounded that place of the Apostle. So sound Prosper: No others will come into the fellowship of the inheritance of Christ than those who before the foundation of the world were elected, and predestinated and foreknown according to the purpose of him who works all things according to the counsel of his will. If therefore certain infants are gifted with the heavenly inheritance, the same also are predestinated or elected.
pass_b_english: Prosper agrees (On Free Choice): in infants neither prior nor later devotion is chosen — he means those reborn as soon as born, and snatched from this life into eternal beatitude. Grevinchovius (Disputation on Election from foresighted faith, p. 143), caught by this, finally doubts whether there is any infant election at all. But whoever has eternal life surely has election to eternal life — the glorified do not outnumber the predestined. Whom he predestined, them he glorified, and no others (so Augustine on the Apostle). Sound Prosper: none enter Christ's inheritance but those elected before the world's foundation, predestined and foreknown according to his purpose. If some infants receive the heavenly inheritance, those same are predestined or elect.
source_text: Cui suffragatur Prosper in lib. De libero arbitrio: In infantibus nec praecedens eligitur nec secutura devotio. De his loquor qui mox ut nati sunt renascuntur, et rapti ab hac vita aeternae beatitudini deputantur. Grevinchovius in Disputatione de Electione ex fide praevisa, pag. 143, hoc argumento irretitus, eo tandem delabitur, ut in dubium vocet utrum sit ulla infantium electio necne. Sed quorum est vita aeterna, illorum proculdubio est electio ad vitam aeternam, cum numerus glorificatorum numerum praedestinatorum sive electorum non excedat. Nam quos praedestinavit glorificavit, et non alios, ut recte Augustinus illum locum Apostoli exposuit. Sic sanus Prosper: Non alii venient in consortium haereditatis Christi, quam qui ante constitutionem mundi electi sunt, et praedestinati atque praesciti secundum propositum ejus, qui omnia operatur secundum consilium voluntatis suae. Si ergo quidam infantes haereditate caelesti donantur, iidem etiam praedestinantur sive eliguntur.
